title: Beats 360 modüler yapısı ve kablosuz mimarisiyle tanıtıldı
summary: Beats'in yeni kulak üstü modeli Beats 360, değiştirilebilir yastıkları, IPX4 suya dayanıklılığı ve kablosuz iç mimarisiyle öne çıkıyor.
body:
Beats, yeni kulak üstü kulaklık modeli **Beats 360** ile kullanıcı karşısına çıktı. Tasarımında kişiselleştirilebilir parçalara odaklanan ürün, hem antrenmanlarda hem de günlük kullanımda rahatlık sağlamak amacıyla geliştirildi.

## Beats 360 neler sunuyor?

Beats 360, markanın önceki modellerine kıyasla daha dengeli bir ağırlık dağılımı hedefliyor. Kulaklık, 294,5 gram ağırlığa sahip olmasına karşın hafif kafa bandı yapısıyla konforu artırıyor. Cihazda iki farklı kulak yastığı seçeneği sunuluyor: Ter emici dokuma iplikten üretilen Performance Knit ve daha sıkı yalıtım sunan sentetik deri UltraPlush. IPX4 suya dayanıklılık sertifikası bulunan kulaklık, spor salonundaki terlemelere ve hafif yağmura karşı direnç gösteriyor.

Modelin donanım mimarisi de dikkat çekiyor. Kablosuz kulak içi kulaklıklara benzer şekilde her iki kulaklık kapağında ayrı pil, anten ve işlemci barındıran tamamen kablosuz bir yapı kullanılıyor. Ses kontrolleri kulaklığın arka yüzündeki fiziksel düğmelere taşınırken, cihaz Bluetooth 5.3 üzerinden bağlantı kuruyor. Alt kısımdaki USB-C yuvası yalnızca şarj amacıyla kullanılıyor; 3,5 mm jak girişi veya kablolu ses desteği bulunmuyor.

## Ekosistem uyumu ve ses özellikleri

Beats 360, gücünü markanın dördüncü nesil özel çipinden alıyor. Bu çip sayesinde kulaklık hem iOS hem de Android cihazlarla doğrudan uyumlu çalışıyor. Kulaklıkta dinamik kafa takibi özellikli kişiselleştirilmiş uzamsal ses ve kafa yapısına göre sesi ayarlayan Adaptive EQ modu bulunuyor. Cihaz ayrıca **Apple Bul** ve Google Find Hub ağları üzerinden konum takibini destekliyor. ABD pazarında 350 dolarlık liste fiyatıyla satışa sunulan modelin Türkiye fiyatı henüz açıklanmadı.

**Neden önemli?** Beats, uzun bir aradan sonra sunduğu modüler yastık tasarımı ve bağımsız donanım mimarisiyle hem Apple hem de Android kullanıcılarını hedefleyen esnek bir seçenek sunuyor.

Beats 360 are the Beats over-ear headphones I've always wanted, but they're no Studio Pro
Oct 8, 2026 — 5:48 PM ET
Beats 360
Weight: 295g
Beats carved out a niche for itself in the midrange audio market, delivering popular headphone models like the Studio Pro and Solo 4. Each of those models was a tasteful tweak to the familiar Studio and Solo product lines, but it’s been a while since we saw a genuinely new pair of headphones from Beats. That changes with the Beats 360, a completely fresh pair of over-ear headphones designed to be customized with colorful ear cushions and headband inserts.
The Beats 360 are stylish, comfortable, water-resistant, and as versatile as any pair of over-ear headphones I’ve tested. They can handle a gym workout, a daily commute, and almost everything in between. The one thing the Beats 360 can’t handle is wired lossless audio, as these headphones use a truly wireless connectivity architecture. Are the design and comfort of the Beats 360 worth the sound quality trade-offs? Here’s what I learned after nearly two weeks of testing these $350 cans.
This article was published on Sept 30, 2026, and has been updated as follows:
- October 8, 2026: added measurements, Multi-Dimensional Audio Quality Scores, microphone samples, preliminary review scores.
What’s it like to use the Beats 360?
The Beats 360 are a pair of lifestyle headphones with swappable ear cushions and headbands, complete with IPX4 water resistance and the ultimate customization experience.
Design
Beats 360 slot into the brand’s headphone lineup at the Studio Pro’s old price, and they solve key design issues with the 2023 over-ear headphones. While the Beats Studio Pro were over-ear headphones, they had tiny ear cushions, and barely any padding on the headband.
Unlike the AirPods Max, the headband cushion on the Beats Studio Pro can be replaced when it wears out, but there’s no fixing the comfort issues if they don’t fit your head shape well. The Beats 360, with a lightweight headband, swappable cushions, and better weight balance, finally solves these problems.
The modular design of the Beats 360 requires the over-ear headphones to be absurdly compact with the cushions removed. These headphones have a cylindrical plastic headband that connects the two audio drivers. The curved shape extends throughout the Beats 360’s design.
Beats offers ear cushion materials for the 360 headphones: Performance Knit and UltraPlush. The latter is the eco-leather material we’ve seen on prior Beats headphones, but the former is a new textile-thread material designed to absorb sweat. I’ve worn the Beats 360 for nearly two weeks, and one thing’s for certain — the ear cushions you choose matter (more than it looks like on the chart, anyway). The eco-leather UltraPlush cushions practically stick to your face, creating a strong seal and quite a bit of pressure. The Beats 360 have a stronger clamping force. Paired with the tight UltraPlush seal and strong ANC pressure, you may experience discomfort. The Performance Knit cushions are more comfortable in this regard.
I’ve tested both cushion types with the Beats 360, and it’s easy to see where each one shines. The UltraPlush cushions create a tight seal against your head — even for people wearing glasses or facial hair — which is better for active noise canceling.
Meanwhile, the Performance Knit are undoubtedly more comfortable and are better at wicking moisture away. This is crucial because the Beats 360 are IPX4 water-resistant. You can wear these headphones at the gym or during a drizzle and be just fine.
The Beats 360 weigh 294.5 grams, so they’re not the lightest headphones on the market. They are actually heavier than the Studio Pro, but the Beats 360 feel more comfortable to wear due to the lightweight headband. Almost all the headphone’s components are stashed inside the ear cups, as the Beats 360 uses a truly wireless design. Like wireless earbuds, the Beats 360 have a separate battery, antenna, and processor in each ear cup, enabling this balanced and modular design.
Beats finally shifted the on-headphone controls to the back side of the 360. Typically, Beats headphones have used the Beats logo on the side of an ear cup for controls, and this means you’re pushing into your head to change the volume or press play on a track. This time, the Beats 360 have a volume rocker and playback control button on the back side of the right ear cup, and a button that cycles through ANC modes on the back side of the left ear cup.
There’s also a power and Bluetooth pairing button that sits flush with the Beats 360 chassis on the back side of the left ear cup. Since it’s the only button that doesn’t protrude from the Beats 360, you won’t accidentally press it while reaching for the ANC button. However, this makes it hard to find with your fingers, and on my black Beats 360 review unit, it’s also hard to see in the dark.
Finally, there’s a single USB-C port on the bottom of the left ear cup. This is unfortunately only for power and charging. Without USB audio support or a 3.5mm jack, there’s no way to use the Beats 360 over a cable.
Features
The Beats 360 are powered by the brand’s fourth-generation proprietary chip, which integrates natively with iOS and Android. Android users can connect to and manage their Beats 360 headphones in the Beats app, while iPhone users can do the same in the Settings app.
Beats 360 support Personalized Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking, but you need an iPhone with a TrueDepth camera to set it up. After configuring Personalized Spatial Audio for the first time, your custom profile will be synced between your Apple devices. However, it’s unavailable on Android and other third-party Bluetooth devices.
The headphones miss out on a custom equalizer. Instead, they have a single Adaptive EQ mode, which tunes the sound to your specific fit and ear seal rather than using a standardized preset — just like the AirPods Max does. Adaptive EQ only works when both ANC and transparency mode are off, and that Off setting isn’t available on the headphones by default. You’ll need to enable it in your iPhone’s Settings app, System Settings on a Mac, or the Beats app on Android before the listening mode button will cycle to it. Apple’s support page walks through the steps. It would’ve been nice to have manual EQ controls in addition to Adaptive EQ, though.
Beyond spatial audio and the Adaptive EQ mode, the Beats 360 are light on audio features. The headphones do support Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub for tracking, and work with automatic switching on Apple and Android devices. Finally, you can use the Beats app for Android to add a battery and noise control widget to your home screen.
